links.outcome: Effect of requiring verbatim supporting quotes on coverage, macro-F1, and semantic support of quotes
links.effect: Quotes mechanically valid in 83.3% to 91.2% of runs, but only 48.0% to 78.8% judged semantically supported. Coverage fell slightly; macro-F1 changed by model (gains for GPT-5.2 and Gemini, decrease for Claude).
links.quote: Mechanically valid quotes occurred in 83.3% to 91.2% of runs, yet only 48.0% to 78.8% of evidence-bearing predictions were judged semantically supported.

links.outcome: Label stability across three repeated runs per abstract
links.effect: Labels were stable across repetitions, with Fleiss' kappa 0.829 to 0.969.
links.quote: Labels were stable across repetitions (Fleiss' kappa 0.829 to 0.969).

unlisted_practices: Mechanically verifiable verbatim-quote requirement for LLM outputs, with an LLM judge rating quote support
Restricting automation to predictions with semantically supported evidence (selective automation)

screen.practice: verbatim quote evidence requirement and mechanical validation
screen.reason: Empirical benchmark testing a deployment safeguard/guardrail (requiring mechanically verifiable verbatim quotes alongside LLM classifications to enable automated auditing and selective abstention) compared to standard label-only outputs.
